1.title: Identify what sensors must measure
1.intro: Industrial sensors turn physical conditions into numbers used for control and safety.
pts: Common signals: temperature, pressure, flow, level, vibration, gas.
Match accuracy, range and environment to the job: heat, wash-down, dust, explosive atmosphere.
Ask users what a wrong reading costs and what accuracy they need.
Pick one sensor type for your first product.
1.ex: A cold-room temperature sensor needs plus or minus 0.5 degrees C from -30 to +10; wrong readings spoil stock worth 40,000.
1.act: Interview three plant users and write a requirement sheet.

2.title: Know product safety and approval rules
2.intro: Industrial products must be safe and legal.
pts: Electrical safety approvals by an accredited body are normally required.
Equipment for explosive atmospheres needs special certification.
2.ex: Row: 'Sell a sensor into a gas plant | hazardous-location certification | certify | before sale | certificate'.
2.act: Build a rules table for one sensor.

3.title: Design, build and calibrate
3.intro: Accuracy comes from design and calibration.
pts: Choose a sensing element and a stable circuit.
Calibrate at several points against a reference.
Test for temperature drift and noise.
Write the data sheet from measured results.
3.ex: Reference 20.00; sensor reads 20.4 at three points; offset corrected; error after calibration plus or minus 0.1.
3.act: Calibrate a sensor at three points and record error.

4.title: Cost and price the product
pts: Parts, assembly, test and calibration time.
4.ex: Price 145; cost 70; margin 75 (52%); fixed cost 150,000 → break-even 2,000 sensors. Teaching figures in CAD.
4.act: Build cost sheet with low-volume case.

5.title: Control production quality
5.ex: Yield 94%; main fail: solder joint; fix: reflow profile.

6.title: Sell and support
pts: Provide integration notes for common controllers.

7.title: Manage cyber and safety risk
7.ex: Risk: 'Default password found | 3 x 5 | unique keys | firmware lead | each release'.

8.title: Pilot with a customer
pts: Stop rule: drift above spec means redesign.
